__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: The Prometheus-compatible datasource (Mimir, Grafana Cloud, a local Prometheus scraping an OTel Collector, ...) that receives striker's OTLP metrics - see backend/README.md's "OpenTelemetry metrics" section.

title: Striker - game activity & economy
description: Every OpenTelemetry metric striker's svc/engine export - see backend/README.md's "OpenTelemetry metrics" section and backend/common/telemetry.go for the source of truth. Import into Grafana (Dashboards > New > Import), pick the Prometheus-compatible datasource that receives striker's OTLP metrics when prompted, and turn export on with OTEL_METRICS_ENABLED=true (see the README) for panels to show data. The "Per node" row (filterable by the job / instance variables) needs a backend that ingests OTLP natively (Prometheus >=2.47, Mimir, Grafana Cloud) so the service.instance.id resource attribute becomes the `instance` label used there.

panels.title: HTTP error rate (4xx)
panels.description: Share of requests answered with a 4xx status. A jump on one route usually means a client bug or a broken link, not a server fault - see the 5xx panels for those.

panels.title: Top 10 routes by 5xx responses (selected range)
panels.description: The ten routes that returned the most 5xx responses over the dashboard's time range. Empty means no server errors.

panels.title: HTTP request duration (p50 / p95)
panels.description: Overall latency without the live-match websockets (routes ending in /live), which stay open for the whole match. Series exported before the svc stopped timing websocket upgrades are filtered out by the route.

panels.title: HTTP request duration (p95, by route)
panels.description: p95 latency of every route except the live-match websockets (routes ending in /live).

panels.title: Match backlog (overdue / in simulation)
panels.description: Overdue: unplayed matches with both teams set whose kickoff passed more than 5 minutes ago (a cup bye is never counted). In simulation: matches an engine replica has claimed and not finished. Every engine replica reports the same DB-wide value, so this uses max, never sum. A line that stays above 0 means the engine is not keeping up (or is down).

panels.title: Seconds since each job last finished
panels.description: Time since any replica last finished each job. The 300 s line matters for the jobs that run every minute (simulate_matches, cups, friendlies); daily and weekly jobs naturally sit far above it, which is why the axis is logarithmic.

panels.title: Engine job duration (p95)
panels.description: p95 of how long one scheduled run of each job takes.

panels.title: Claims won per replica (per day)
panels.description: Once-per-period claims each engine replica won in the last day. A replica that never wins shows at 0 while the other shows every claim, which tells you the work is not being shared.

panels.title: Job runs per replica (per hour)
panels.description: Times each job fired on each replica. A run that lost its claim still counts here: it shows the trigger fired on that replica; the claims panel shows who did the work.

panels.title: Matches simulated per day, by competition type
Goals scored per day, by competition type
Academy promotions per day
panels.description: Youth academy prospects promoted to the senior squad - see AcademyPromotionsCounter in backend/common/telemetry.go.

panels.title: Goals per match, by competition type
panels.description: Goals divided by matches simulated over 1 h windows (both counters carry the competition type). The reason striker.goals.scored exists: a quick check that the match engine has not drifted.

panels.title: Transfers completed vs. free agent signings (per day)
Money credited per day, by reason
panels.description: Everything the ledger credited to teams, per day, stacked by TRANSACTION_* reason.

panels.title: Money debited per day, by reason
panels.description: Everything the ledger debited from teams, per day, stacked by reason.

panels.title: Net money created per day
panels.description: Credited minus debited per day, leaving out transfer_in, transfer_out and loan_fee: those move money between teams and net to zero. Positive means the economy is inflating (sponsors, prizes, ticket sales outpace wages and upkeep).

panels.title: Total money in the economy (trend)
panels.description: The same figure as the stat in the Economy row, over time. It should move by the net creation panel above.

panels.title: Transfer offers made vs. resolved, by outcome (per day)
CPU market actions per day, by action
panels.description: What CPU teams do on the transfer market: signings, purchases, offers, listings.

panels.title: Notifications sent per day, by type
Live match viewers
panels.description: Live-match websockets currently open on each svc instance.

panels.title: Web push outcomes per day
panels.description: sent: the push service accepted it. expired: the subscription was gone (404/410) and was deleted. failed: a transport error or any other status (429, 5xx, ...); these are not retried.

panels.title: DB connections (in use / idle)
panels.description: database/sql pool state per process. The pool is capped at 50 connections per process: in use sitting at the cap means requests are queueing for a connection.

panels.title: DB connection waits per second
panels.description: How often a caller had to wait for a free connection. Should sit at 0.

panels.title: DB connection wait time
panels.description: Seconds spent waiting for a connection per second of wall time, summed over callers.

panels.title: HTTP requests per node (svc)
panels.description: Each svc replica's own request rate, labeled by the service.instance.id resource attribute (Prometheus/Mimir's `instance` label) - see backend/common/telemetry.go's InitMetrics doc comment. Flat, overlapping lines mean the load balancer is spreading traffic evenly across replicas; one line riding well above the rest means it isn't.

panels.title: HTTP request share per node (svc)
panels.description: Same data as "HTTP requests per node", normalized to each node's percentage of total traffic right now - makes uneven distribution obvious even while overall load is changing (e.g. during a deploy's rolling restart).

panels.title: Matches simulated per node (engine)
panels.description: Each engine replica's own share of match simulation work, labeled by `instance` (service.instance.id) - lets you check whether simulation jobs are actually spread across replicas or piling onto one.

panels.title: Matches simulated share per node (engine)
panels.description: Same data as "Matches simulated per node", normalized to each node's percentage of simulated matches right now.

panels.title: Goroutines per node
panels.description: Live goroutines in each svc/engine replica right now - see striker.process.goroutines in backend/common/telemetry.go. Unlike the other "Per node" panels this covers both services at once (every process registers it), so each line is labeled by both job (service.name: svc/engine) and instance so you can tell which is which. A line climbing steadily rather than settling into a steady-state band usually means a goroutine leak.

panels.title: Heap memory per node
panels.description: Bytes of heap memory each svc/engine replica currently has allocated and in use - see striker.process.memory.heap_alloc in backend/common/telemetry.go. Labeled by job and instance, same as "Goroutines per node".

panels.title: CPU usage per node
panels.description: Each svc/engine replica's own CPU time, averaged over a 5m window - see striker.process.cpu_time in backend/common/telemetry.go. 1.0 means fully saturating one core; values above 1.0 are possible for a process using more than one core at once. Linux only (empty if the backend isn't running on Linux).

panels.title: Uptime per node
panels.description: Seconds since each svc/engine replica's process started - see striker.process.uptime in backend/common/telemetry.go. A line that resets to zero is that replica restarting (a crash, an OOM kill, a deploy's rolling restart) - useful for spotting a node that's crash-looping while the others stay up.
